_comment: Portfolio backlog for /agent-loop. Spans THREE repos around one thesis: anvil-engine is the self-hosted agentic browser that BOTH products run on (no Browserbase/Browserless/Steel). Each iteration: STAGE 0 triage across all streams -> do the single highest-leverage item -> verify -> commit/push -> REFILL (append >=1 new next-step you discovered). STOP only if truly nothing + refill yielded nothing.
thesis: anvil-engine (self-hosted CDP browser) is shared infra. Relay = consumer text-a-bot on anvil. DataFaucet = dev/MCP layer; its capture flow still pays Browserbase — moving it to anvil unifies the stack and removes the vendor. Synergy: one browser engine, two products, zero browser vendor.

repos.relay: C:/Users/acwic/relay (awictor/relay, branch main) — consumer Telegram agent. MVP DONE + live-verified.
repos.datafaucet: C:/Users/acwic/mcp-forge (awictor/mcp-forge, master) — DO NOT touch master. All work on branch anvil-migration behind a feature flag; prod stays on Browserbase until Alex merges.
repos.anvil: C:/Users/acwic/anvil-engine (awictor/anvil-engine, main) — the shared browser engine.

invariants: Free services only. Never commit secrets (.env gitignored; grep staged diff before push).

DataFaucet: NEVER commit to master. Use branch 'anvil-migration'; gate every behavior change behind an env flag (e.g. BROWSER_BACKEND=anvil|browserbase, default browserbase) so prod is unaffected until merge.
Verify before done: tsc + tests each repo; real e2e (anvil live at http://localhost:3000) when possible; report call-tested honestly.
$? after a pipe is the pipe's status. Context-mode hook blocks curl — use ctx_execute(fetch) for HTTP probes.
EVERY iteration must REFILL: append >=1 concrete next-step to items[] before finishing, so the loop never dead-ends.

streams.synergy: Wire DataFaucet capture-flow (auto-scan) to anvil as an alternative browser backend behind BROWSER_BACKEND flag. This is the flagship cross-product work — deep well: adapter, session mgmt, live-view, tests, parity with Browserbase.
streams.relay: Extend Relay: more channels (SMS/WhatsApp), richer tools, memory persistence, deploy hardening. Also: dogfood — could Relay consume a DataFaucet-hosted MCP?
streams.anvil: Harden the shared engine: whatever both consumers need (stability, stealth, session limits, observability). Fixes here benefit both products.

owner_blockers: deploy-1 (relay): Oracle Always Free VM for 24/7 (DEPLOY.md). Owner-gated.
DataFaucet prod merge: after anvil-migration branch is proven, Alex decides when to merge + flip the flag.

Confirm /v1/metrics exposes session counts + latency both products can monitor; add anything missing. Low priority until a real deploy exists.

Verified live: 17 request headers on a doc fetch. anvil HAR entry shape: {url,method,status,duration,responseSize,timestamp,requestHeaders:{}, requestBody?:string, resourceType}. This gives DataFaucet capture everything it needs (auth headers + POST bodies), unblocking syn-1c.

DONE: switched default model to gemini-flash-lite-latest (higher free cap) + automatic model FAILOVER in GeminiClient — on 429/403 quota it advances through a chain (lite -> flash-latest -> 2.5-flash-lite -> 2.5-flash), each with its own free quota; transient 503/504/500 still retry w/ backoff on the same model. GEMINI_MODELS env overrides the chain. 3 failover unit tests. 23/23 green.

Real gap was analytics leaking via DEV-0008 responseContentType; added NOISE patterns (google collect, segment/amplitude/mixpanel, *.stripe.com, ahrefs, /track, /pixel). 8 filter tests, 10 anvil+filter pass]

Do NOT merge to master — leave for Alex.

Confirm default browserbase 503 still fires when creds missing + flag unset. Wire into test:unit gate. [DONE: tests/integration/anvil-browse.test.ts 4 tests + browser-anvil-lifecycle.test.ts; 10 anvil integration tests green; wired into test:unit]

Live-view interactivity: anvil /v1/view is read-only MJPEG (no click injection like Browserbase debugger). Either (a) document the read-only limit in inline-browser.tsx UI when backend=anvil, or (b) add a lightweight click-forward: overlay captures coords -> POST anvil /v1/actions/click-at (needs a new anvil endpoint by pixel). Decide + spec.

Persist per-chat memory across restarts (currently in-memory Map, lost on restart). Simple JSON file or sqlite; bounded. Unit-test load/save. Keeps the agent context after a redeploy. Broaden Relay agent capability beyond browse/scrape: add a structured extract tool (given a URL + a natural-language field list, drive anvil to load the page then return JSON with those fields) so a user can text "get me the price and title from <url>" and get clean data, not prose. Reuse src/anvil.ts readCurrent/scrape; keep the LLM behind the adapter; bound steps; unit-test with a mock BrowserBackend. [DONE: extract tool in src/agent.ts + extractFields() LLM sub-call; ToolSpec extended for array params; 7 tests; 43 suite pass; live e2e anvil+Gemini green]

Add a multi-page extract: let extract accept an array of URLs (or a search-then-extract flow) and return a JSON array, so a user can text "compare the price of X across these 3 links". Reuse extractFields per page; cap page count; dedup; keep steps bounded. Unit-test with mock backend returning distinct pages. [DONE: compare tool in src/agent.ts — multi-URL parallel extract, dedup+SSRF-filter+cap5, all-null row on per-url failure; 4 tests; 47 suite pass; live e2e 2 URLs green]

extractFields currently scrapes text only (document.body.innerText). For data-heavy SPAs the value may be in attributes/meta/JSON-LD. Add an option to also pass the page HTML (or <script type=application/ld+json>) into the extraction prompt when text extraction yields all-null. Guard prompt size. [DONE: anvil.extractStructured (JSON-LD + meta) + extractFieldsResult allNull flag; extract retries structured when text pass all-null; 5 tests; 88 suite pass; live e2e GitHub 3022/MDN 712 chars meta]

Search-then-compare: let the agent take a query (not pre-known URLs), browse a search/listing page, harvest the top N result links (reuse the link-discovery evaluate pattern from anvil auto-scan), then compare/extract across them. So a user can text "cheapest 3 listings for <item>" without pasting URLs. Bound N, SSRF-filter harvested links, unit-test with a mock backend that returns a listing page + child pages. [DONE: anvil.discoverLinks + search tool; same-host-preferred, SSRF-filtered, capped 20; 4 tests; 51 suite pass; live e2e 37 hrefs from HN]

Full search->compare live e2e: script a real agent run (mock or real LLM) that calls search on a listing page then compare on 2-3 harvested links, asserting a final JSON array with fields. Proves the whole no-URL-needed flow end to end (unit tests cover the pieces; this covers the chain).

Update /help + /start (src/commands.ts) and README to advertise the new capabilities (extract, compare, search) with example texts a user can send (e.g. "extract the price and title from <url>", "compare price across these 3 links", "find newest HN posts about X"). Keeps the product legible to real users now that it does more than scrape. [DONE: /start + /help advertise extract/compare/search with example texts; README gains What-you-can-text-it section; commands test green]

Reply formatting for SMS: extract/compare return JSON to the model, but the user gets a phone text. Add guidance (system prompt) + a light post-format so compare results become a short readable list (e.g. "A: $10 | B: $20") not raw JSON, and long extracts get trimmed. Unit-test a formatter that turns a compare JSON array into <=N lines. Keep it deterministic + LLM-agnostic. [DONE: src/lib/format-reply.ts renders stray JSON->lines, trims to phone size; wired into index.ts + system prompt; 9 tests; 64 suite pass]

Single integration test that runs a scripted-LLM agent through search->compare->reply and asserts the FINAL formatReply output is readable lines (not JSON), proving the tools + formatter compose. Ties together relay-search-e2e intent with the new formatter. Offline (mock backend + scripted LLM). [DONE: test/agent-chain.test.ts — search->compare->reply composition + lazy-model JSON-reply rendered as lines; 2 tests; 66 suite pass]

Speed up the anvil crawl test (syn-1i runs ~12s): the route sleeps 1200ms/page to let XHRs fire. Make that settle interval configurable via env (e.g. ANVIL_CRAWL_SETTLE_MS, default 1200) so the mock test can set it to ~0 and run in <1s. Keep prod default unchanged. Then the whole anvil suite is CI-fast. [DONE: ANVIL_CRAWL_SETTLE_MS env (default 1200, prod unchanged); tests set 0 -> crawl+capture ~14s to ~1.25s]

Concurrent-loop work (DEV-0008) is UNCOMMITTED on anvil-migration: modified auto-scan/route.ts + capture-filter.ts + anvil-capture.test.ts to capture API requests by responseContentType (JSON response header) not just request markers. Verify that change: run its test, tsc, confirm browserbase path unchanged, then commit it to anvil-migration (do NOT leave dirty). If broken, fix or revert. [DONE (moot): DEV-0008 was committed by its own loop (a3672f93); branch clean, verified green]

Optional capture polish: the capture check-regex in verification over-flagged api.paritydeals.com (a real third-party deals API on reqres.in) as noise-ish. It was correctly KEPT by the actual filter (only a test-harness heuristic flagged it). Decide + document; low priority.

Add a direct http/JSON-API tool: many user asks (weather, prices, sports) are answered by a public JSON API faster than driving a browser. Add a fetch_json(url) tool (SSRF-guarded, size-capped, JSON-only content-type, no secrets forwarded) so the agent can hit an API directly and extract from the JSON, falling back to scrape/browse for HTML sites. Unit-test with a mock fetch; keep it behind the same safety guards. [DONE: fetch_json tool — SSRF-guarded, 200KB cap, JSON-content-type required, no creds forwarded, injectable; 4 tests; 70 suite pass; live e2e real GitHub API JSON 200]

Now that the agent has scrape/browse/extract/compare/search/fetch_json, add a couple of routing regression tests (scripted LLM) asserting the SYSTEM_PROMPT guidance leads to sensible tool choice on representative asks (weather -> fetch_json/scrape, price+title -> extract, multi-link -> compare). Not testing the model, testing that the tool set + descriptions are coherent + the loop dispatches each correctly. Guards against tool-wiring regressions as tools grow. [DONE: test/agent-dispatch.test.ts — tool-surface (10 names + valid desc/params) + per-tool dispatch to backend; 8 tests; 78 suite pass]

Relay is feature-complete (6 fetch tools, memory, safety, SMS formatting, 78 tests) but only runs on Alex machine. [OWNER ACTION] Provision Oracle Cloud Always Free VM + run stack per DEPLOY.md (docker compose up -d). Only Alex can create the VM + hold the 3 secrets. Then loop can do a real inbound-text e2e. Last step to live-for-users.

Wire the same JSON-LD/meta fallback into the compare tool (per-URL): compare currently calls extractFields (text only). Refactor its per-row extraction to reuse the extract handler path (text -> structured fallback) so multi-page compares also benefit on SPA/product pages. Keep parallel fetch + all-null-row-on-failure. Add a test. [DONE: shared extractOne() helper; extract+compare both text->JSON-LD/meta fallback; per-row, only when text all-null; 1 test; 89 suite pass]

Resilience: a single anvil hiccup (session create/navigate timeout) currently fails a scrape/extract outright. Add one bounded retry (backoff) around the anvil scrape/navigate in src/anvil.ts for transient errors (timeout, ECONNRESET, 5xx) — NOT for SSRF/4xx. Cap attempts, keep total time sane. Unit-test with a mock that fails once then succeeds. [DONE: withRetry wraps createSession+action; transient (timeout/ECONNRESET/5xx/408/429) retried w/ backoff, deterministic (SSRF/4xx) throws; ANVIL_RETRY_ATTEMPTS env; isTransientError exported+tested; 3 tests; 92 suite pass; live scrape ok]

Lightweight per-turn observability: index.ts already logs [in]. Add a one-line [out] log per turn with steps taken, tools used (names), elapsed ms, and reply length (redacted) so a 24/7 deploy is debuggable from logs alone. runAgent already returns steps; thread back the tool-name list. Keep it structured (JSON line) + secret-redacted. Unit-test the log formatting. [DONE: runAgent returns tools[]; index.ts logs [out] JSON per turn (steps/tools/ms/replyChars/ok/error, no content/secrets); src/lib/turn-log.ts; 4 tests; 96 suite pass]

In-memory rolling counters from the per-turn data (total turns, ok/fail, avg steps, tool-use histogram, p50/p95 ms) exposed via a tiny /healthz-style log-on-signal or a periodic summary line every N turns, so operator sees aggregate health without parsing every [out] line. Pure counter module + unit test; wire a summary log every 50 turns in index.ts. [DONE: src/lib/metrics.ts Metrics (turns/ok/fail/avgSteps/tool-histogram/p50/p95 via 500-sample ring); index.ts records+[metrics] every RELAY_METRICS_EVERY(50); 5 tests; 101 suite pass]

Update the README status/architecture to reflect the shipped reality: 6 fetch tools (scrape/browse/extract/compare/search/fetch_json) + JSON-LD fallback, persistent memory, safety caps, SMS formatting, transient retry, per-turn [out] + [metrics] observability, 101 tests. Small doc-accuracy fix so the repo represents itself correctly to Alex/readers. [DONE: README Status + run note + architecture updated to shipped reality (6 tools, retry, memory, SMS format, [out]/[metrics], 101 tests, DEPLOY.md); suite 101 pass]

Prove memory persistence survives a real restart: script that (1) MemoryStore.set(chatA, turns) -> new MemoryStore instance on same file -> assert get(chatA) returns the turns (simulates process restart). Unit-level already covers load/save; this asserts the cross-instance file round-trip explicitly. Offline, no Telegram. src/index.ts (the message handler wiring: command check -> rate limit -> agent -> formatReply -> memory.set -> [out]/[metrics]) has no direct test. Extract the per-message handler into a testable function (deps injected: llm, memory, sendMessage, sendTyping) and unit-test the wiring: a command short-circuits the agent, a rate-limited chat gets the limit msg, a normal msg records a turn + persists memory. Offline.

User hit "operation aborted due to timeout". Root cause: anvil REST /v1/scrape + navigate hardcoded networkidle2 (60s cap) which hangs on polling sites like HN. Fixed relay scrape() to navigate(domcontentloaded)+readCurrent and defaulted navigate to domcontentloaded. HN scrape 15s->1.1s. Worker restarted with fix. (Separately, Gemini free tier 429 quota from heavy testing — retry/backoff already handles it.)
Gemini free-tier quota exhausted on flash. Fix: default to -lite (higher cap) + automatic failover chain on 429 across independent-quota models. 3 tests. Worker restarted.
